$description: Dipia design tokens. Generated from src/app/globals.css -- that file is the source of truth; this is a portable mirror for design tools. Light-only: there is no dark theme, and `--dark` below is a surface, not a mode. All colours are sRGB hex.

meta.tagline: A simulation engine for human relationships.
meta.wordmark: dipia (always lowercase, one word, tight tracking -- the wordmark IS the logo)
meta.world: Life-sim, warm and playful: pixel-art sprites over clean modern UI. The pixel lives in the ART -- avatars, venue, board. Type and controls stay crisp.
meta.stack: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first @theme, no config file), shadcn/ui on Radix, lucide icons
meta.livingReference: /design -- every token, every lens, every component state, rendered
meta.replaces: The earlier dark system (brand cyan, OKLCH, Instrument Serif + Geist, .glow). Removed in commit d6e0d4d. Nothing from it is current.

theme.$description: There is no `.dark` block. The `dark` custom-variant stays DECLARED because the shadcn primitives in src/components/ui/** carry 44 `dark:` utilities and an undeclared variant is a build error -- with no `.dark` ancestor they simply never match, which is what a light-only theme wants. Never add a dark palette without deciding it as a product change first.

background.$description: Warm cream. The ground for every screen.

card.$description: Raised surface. Barely lighter than the ground -- separation comes from the shadow, not from contrast.

surface-alt.$description: Recessed / secondary fill: muted chips, inactive tabs, sprite tiles.

dark.$description: NOT a theme. The room's night canvas (screen 1b) -- the one deliberately dark surface in the product.

foreground.$description: Warm dark brown, never black. Body and headings.

ink-faint.$description: Eyebrows, disabled labels, the quietest legible step.

primary-shadow.$description: The toy shadow's colour. Follows the lens -- this is what makes the whole depth system retint for free.

primary-tint.$description: Quiet fill for secondary buttons and pills.

brand.$description: Deliberately the same coral as --primary. Use --brand for a mark that must NOT follow the lens.

destructive.$description: Distinct from coral on purpose: a destructive action must not read as a primary one when both are warm reds.

friction.$description: Amber. The timeline's 'roce' family. Reserved -- see rules.frictionIsAmber.

border.$description: Hairline, tinted with the ink hue rather than grey.

tag.$description: Timeline event types. All desaturated to the same level so none shouts louder than another in a long list.

lens.$description: The three compatibility lenses. Put the class on any subtree and every token inside it retakes its temperature -- INCLUDING shadow-toy, because that shadow reads from --primary-shadow. One class, no conditional rules.

romantic.$description: Resolves to the same coral as :root by design -- coral IS the romantic accent in this system, not a separate brand hue.

business.$description: Violet, lifted from the timeline's HITO tag.

friendship.$description: Green, lifted from the timeline's MASCOTA tag. Deliberately NOT amber -- see rules.frictionIsAmber.

display.$description: Rounded, heavy, friendly. Headings, the wordmark, CTAs. --font-heading points here too, so shadcn's Card, Dialog and Sheet titles inherit the display voice for free. h1/h2/h3 get font-display + font-extrabold + tracking-tight in @layer base, so a bare heading is already right.

sans.$description: Body, labels, option text. Set on html in @layer base.

mono.$description: Data, ids, option keys, eyebrow labels. No webfont -- the system stack is deliberate.

radius.$description: Every step derives from --radius, so changing one value rescales the whole system.

shadow.$description: THE SIGNATURE OF THIS SYSTEM. A hard offset block: no blur, no spread. It does not imitate light, it imitates one physical object resting on another. toy and toy-lg read from --primary-shadow, so they retint with the lens.

toy.$description: Buttons, selected cards, the brand dot.

card.$description: Neutral resting depth for cards that are not selected.

press.$description: Not a token -- a pattern. A pressed control moves down and loses its shadow, so the object touches the table: translateY(4px) + 0 0 0 var(--primary-shadow).

spacing.$description: Layout rhythm lands on multiples of 8px: section gaps, card padding, stack spacing. In Tailwind's 4px scale that means EVEN steps -- gap-2 (8), gap-4 (16), gap-6 (24), gap-8 (32), p-4, space-y-6. 4px steps are allowed only for optical detail inside a component: the gap between an icon and its label, a badge's inner padding.
spacing.warning: --spacing is deliberately NOT redefined. Tailwind v4 derives the whole scale from it, so setting it to 0.5rem would double every existing p-* and gap-* in the app at once.

pixelArt.$description: Sprites are authored at small pixel dimensions and scaled up. Without image-rendering: pixelated the browser smooths them into mush and the whole visual premise dies.

motion.$description: The room is alive or it is a screenshot. Both beats are decoration, so both stop entirely under prefers-reduced-motion -- a room that jitters is not worth a vestibular migraine.

idle-hop.$description: Idle hop, 2.4-4.5s, staggered per sprite so the crowd never pulses in unison. The stagger comes from the placement -- each Placement carries its own idleDelay.

hop-big.$description: A bigger hop on hover -- the sprite saying 'pick me'.

components.$description: shadcn/ui on Radix, in src/components/ui/**. That directory is shadcn-owned and lint-exempt: never edit it. Compose these into src/components/<feature>/.
notInstalled: form -- the registry replaced it with `field`

rules.rule: No raw hex anywhere in app code. Not in a style prop, not in an arbitrary value like bg-[#0ff]. Tokens in src/app/globals.css are the only styling source. ESLint errors on it.
eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss reads globals.css as the Tailwind v4 entry point, so bg-brand-500 fails if the token is not real.
Amber (#e0a13f) means friction / 'roce' on the timeline. Never reuse it for a lens or a positive state -- friendship is green precisely so the warmest relationship does not read as conflict.
Destructive is #9a2b1e, not the coral. Two warm reds that mean opposite things must not be the same value.
Depth is a hard offset block. No blur, no spread, no soft drop shadows anywhere in the UI. The one blurred shadow in the system is on pixel sprites, and that is art, not chrome.
A card at rest carries shadow-card (neutral) or nothing. shadow-toy is for the selected, hovered or active state -- it is how the system says 'this one'.
Never hard-code a lens colour. Put .lens-* on the subtree and let the tokens cascade, so shadows, rings and tints all move together.
There is no dark theme. --dark is the room's night canvas, a surface. Do not add a .dark palette without deciding it as a product change.
Pixel rendering belongs to sprites and illustration. Type, controls and layout stay crisp -- the contrast between the two is the whole look.

openProblems.problem: The quiz option card is text-only since D14 cancelled per-option images. The 2x2 grid was art-directed around illustrations; what a text card looks like at that size, with four of them on a 390px phone, is not settled. See CLAUDE_DESIGN_QUIZ_BLOCK.md.
The room canvas (--dark) has to hold ~100 sprites on a phone without becoming noise. Placement, scale and idle stagger are the levers.
The AI-offspring reveal has no design yet. It is the emotional peak of the demo and currently a blank.
